history.dynasty: Sikkimese Chogyal period (site sacred since the 18th century)
history.period: Dorje Ling monastery founded 1765 by Lama Dorjey Rinzing; three Shiva lingams said to have self-manifested 1782; monastery destroyed in Gorkha invasion ~1815, relocated to Bhutia Busty 1861; present Mahakal temple built over the self-manifested lingams
history.summary: Identity CONFIRMED: the famous Hindu-Buddhist syncretic shrine atop Observatory Hill, Darjeeling. The site was a sacred spot of the aboriginal Lepcha people, then the Dorje Ling Buddhist monastery (built 1765 by Lama Dorjey Rinzing - the monastery whose name 'Dorjeling' gave Darjeeling its name). Legend says three Shiva lingams (Brahma, Vishnu, Maheshwara) self-manifested here in 1782; after the Gorkha invasion destroyed the monastery (~1815; rebuilt 1861 and moved to Bhutia Busty), the Mahakal temple rose over the lingams. Today both Hindu priests and Buddhist monks perform rituals side by side - Hindus turn prayer wheels, Buddhists ring temple bells; prayer flags and gongs surround the hilltop shrine. CONFLICT (verify): one source says the temple itself was built 1782 by Lama Dorjey Rinzing; another that a local Hindu king built it after the monastery's destruction. Invasion dates vary: 1788 vs 1815 across sources.

name: Mahakal Temple
town_description: Darjeeling, the 'Queen of the Hills' in the Darjeeling district of West Bengal, sits at about 6,700 ft in the eastern Himalayas. Founded as a British sanatorium and hill station, it is famed for its tea gardens, the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway (toy train), and panoramic views of Kanchenjunga. Observatory Hill rises directly above the town centre (near the Mall/Chowrasta), making Mahakal Temple one of the town's most visited landmarks.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaivism) + Tibetan Buddhism - living syncretic shrine

travel.railway: Darjeeling railway station (toy train) at the base of Observatory Hill; New Jalpaiguri Junction is the nearest major railhead (~88 km, verify)
travel.road: Climb the Mall Road/Chowrasta steps to Observatory Hill, above the town centre; reachable on foot from the Mall

visitor_information.best_time: March-May and September-November for clear skies and Himalayan views; can be visited year-round
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-6:00 PM (verify) - timings reported by one travel source
